# I2C-slave to Wishbone-master bridge project
Implement every file and module in output_contract.json. Read the unchanged original README and declaration-only interfaces. Only the selected independent design and its complete RTL closure are requested; unrelated repository components and FPGA board designs are separate designs. Rising clk edges and synchronous active-high rst apply throughout. Assert reset initially for several clocks. Transfer ready/valid signals only on a rising edge with both asserted; preserve data while stalled. Internal state encoding and buffering may differ, but externally visible data, completion and error semantics must match. Private scoring uses one complete usable upstream testbench per point; vectors inside a bench are not additional points. The original source is withheld. Curator clarifications below supplement the original documents and take precedence where explicitly correcting ambiguity.

Implement i2c_slave_wbm and i2c_slave as one complete I2C-controlled Wishbone bridge. This design is an I2C SLAVE that initiates Wishbone accesses; it is independent of the I2C master controllers, whose traffic direction and external contract are different.

- Read the unchanged original protocol comment block in specification/rtl_protocol_comments.md. Enable the slave with enable and its exact seven-bit device_address; the wrapper sets an all-ones address mask. Filter SCL/SDA input glitches according to FILTER_LEN. Use open-drain outputs and external resolved input feedback. The slave may hold SCL low to wait for its ready/valid data endpoints; never actively drive either serial line high.
- An I2C write begins with a big-endian address prefix (most significant address byte first), followed by data bytes in increasing byte-address order. Stop or repeated-start terminates the write, flushing a partial word. Set the pointer with an address-only write, then issue a repeated-start I2C read to fetch from that location. Data bytes within the bus word are little-endian, starting at the offset encoded by the pointer.
- CURATOR CORRECTION: the upstream comment's formula has an erroneous outer log2. The number of address-prefix bytes is ceil(ADDR_WIDTH_ADJ/8), where ADDR_WIDTH_ADJ=WB_ADDR_WIDTH+log2((WB_DATA_WIDTH/WB_SELECT_WIDTH)/8). For the qualified eight-bit-byte,16-bit-address configuration, this is exactly TWO address bytes, not one. Use the adjusted width for general declaration parameters.
- Coalesce writes to one aligned bus word until that word is complete or I2C terminates. Drive byte selects only for received bytes, leaving neighboring bytes unmodified; unused payload lanes can contain zero. Coalesce reads into one bus read per aligned word and serialize its data bytes. The internal pointer advances at completed bus-word boundaries; do not infer a precise per-byte pointer value after terminating a partial read. Software should set the address prefix before each transfer whose start matters.
- Wishbone emits aligned BYTE addresses on wb_adr_o, not shifted word indices; wb_sel_o enables byte lanes. Assert cyc/stb for an active request, hold address/data/select/WE until ACK, and use ACK to complete writes or capture read data. No bus-error or retry input is provided. The pinned native bench sets WB_ADDR_WIDTH=16 although the source default is32; preserve the declaration default and support the tested override.
- i2c_slave uses AXI-stream-style data ready/valid internally: m_axis_data carries bytes received from I2C with last on transaction end; s_axis_data supplies bytes to transmit. Keep bytes stable while stalled, honor external ACK/NACK and stop/repeated-start events, and release lines when disabled or reset. busy/bus_addressed/bus_active report protocol progress. Reset clears pending protocol/bus-valid state; do not rely on a previously programmed pointer after reset.
- Qualification uses the original32-bit bus data,16-bit byte address and FILTER_LEN=4 wrapper bench plus the separate original i2c_slave bench. Both whole benches are scored, without counting shared core modules or each transfer as additional cases. Non-OKAY bus responses are not independently verified by these normal-transfer tests.

Original-document scope: unchanged README and original source protocol documentation. Corrections and detailed signal semantics above are explicit curator review against pinned RTL, not model-produced specifications. Simulation-only parameter diagnostics are removed from normalized RTL where present; original source is retained privately.

Simulation I/O, delays, force/release, final blocks and external includes are forbidden. Constant elaboration functions ($clog2, $unsigned, $signed, $bits) and synthesizable storage initialization are permitted. Save all RTL under the exact required paths; only those files are collected.
